findings: Non-blocking: acquisition identity binding is observational only — run() records acquisition_identity.expected_binding_matches (and sha256) but does not fail when identity.json is missing, oversized (>8192), unparseable, or mismatched; enforcement rests entirely on the pinned SIZE/MD5 constants in reviewed source. Receipt consumers must check this field before treating the copy as bound to the acquisition record.

Non-blocking privacy note: candidates() records discovered Drive paths for any directory under MyDrive/Shareddrives containing a file named train.7z, so non-fixed user folder names can enter receipt.json and, via poll, the orchestrator's private status.json. Data stays in user-owned 0600/0700 artifacts, but the poll prompt's claim that the receipt contains only 'fixed paths' slightly overstates.
Non-blocking: MD5 is collision-weak; adequate for corruption/truncation detection of a pinned artifact, not adversarial integrity. The identity.json sha256 recording partially mitigates.

Non-blocking: post-copy verification re-reads the destination through the Drive FUSE mount, which may serve cached bytes; fsync on FUSE is not a cloud-durability guarantee. The receipt caveats capacity measurement similarly but not read-back provenance.

Non-blocking: concurrent or repeated 'start' actions are not deduplicated by the orchestrator; overlapping runs racing candidates() could each produce a 99GB Drive copy (duplicate quota use, no data loss, no overwrite). Only the prompt-level 'Never retry a start' instruction guards this.

Non-blocking: verify_poll's canonical = rstrip('\n') tolerates any number of trailing newlines, marginally broader than the 'terminal LF' docstring; trailing newlines are semantically inert in Python source, so not exploitable. Written-vs-observed equality remains exact.

Non-blocking: orchestrator records actual_models from the worker run but does not enforce claude-fable-5 there (requested via --model); the security-relevant model check for the review artifact is enforced in reviewed().

Scope assumption: verify_cell_sources, tool_exchanges, streams, private_dir, write_private, CPU_CELL, and PRIVATE_CONFIG are imported from modules outside the supplied files and are assumed to behave as previously reviewed; verify_poll's else-branch fails closed on any unexpected operation surfaced by tool_exchanges.

Positive: fail-closed and non-destructive throughout — review gate pins exact file hashes, commit, and response hash; exclusive creation everywhere (mkdir without exist_ok, open('xb')); no delete/overwrite paths; inspect refuses symlinks and files mutated during read; incomplete Drive scan blocks fresh copies; strict job-path regex prevents injection into generated cells; exception text confined to the private console with only the exception class name in the receipt; atomic receipt writes via os.replace; poll binds receipt provenance to the exact reviewed script hash.
